body:
Hello!

Thank you all mini contributors. I'm enjoying switching to this plugin's many modules one by one, and retiring some old, mostly unmaintained VimScript code. I'm having a great time!

Here is a humble suggestion that perhaps could help solve mini.jump2d's issue #354 even if partially (and also relates to #355).

I've basically wanted to configure my usage of the plugin like this:

```lua
MiniJump2d = require('mini.jump2d')
MiniJump2d.setup(MiniJump2d.builtin_opts.single_character)

-- or with more details
MiniJump2d.setup(vim.tbl_deep_extend('force',
    MiniJump2d.builtin_opts.single_character,
    {
        mappings = { start_jumping = '<Leader>j' },
        labels = 'asdfjkl;ghqwertyuiopzxcvbnm,',
        allowed_windows = { current = true, not_current = false, },
    }
))
```

Why? Well, on one hand, seemed more "tidy" and logical. On the other, I've seen that the plugin has this on its source:

```lua
  H.map('n', keymap, MiniJump2d.start, { desc = 'Start 2d jumping' })
  H.map('x', keymap, MiniJump2d.start, { desc = 'Start 2d jumping' })
  -- Use `<Cmd>...<CR>` to have proper dot-repeat
  -- See https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/23406
  -- TODO: use local functions if/when that issue is resolved
  H.map('o', keymap, '<Cmd>lua MiniJump2d.start()<CR>', { desc = 'Start 2d jumping' })
```

So, mapping all the modes myself seemed a bit worse. I'm not sure also of the nuance of this things, as operator pending mode is usually a thing that scares me a bit. :-)

So, the above configuration doesn't work out of the box, but it does work by applying this small patch:

```diff
diff --git i/lua/mini/jump2d.lua w/lua/mini/jump2d.lua
index 633cb11d..6ac0c70d 100644
--- i/lua/mini/jump2d.lua
+++ w/lua/mini/jump2d.lua
@@ -367,7 +367,7 @@ MiniJump2d.start = function(opts)
   local before_start = (opts.hooks or {}).before_start
     or ((vim.b.minijump2d_config or {}).hooks or {}).before_start
     or MiniJump2d.config.hooks.before_start
-  if before_start ~= nil then before_start() end
+  if before_start ~= nil then before_start(opts) end
 
   opts = H.get_config(opts)
   opts.spotter = opts.spotter or MiniJump2d.default_spotter
@@ -667,11 +667,12 @@ local function user_input_opts(input_fun)
     allowed_lines = { blank = false, fold = false },
   }
 
-  local before_start = function()
+  local before_start = function(options)
     local input = input_fun()
     -- Allow user to cancel input and not show any jumping spots
     if input == nil then return end
     res.spotter = MiniJump2d.gen_spotter.pattern(vim.pesc(input))
+    if options then options.spotter = res.spotter end
   end
   res.hooks = { before_start = before_start }
 
```

I *think* this should be backwards compatible, as it is just adding a new parameter that did not exist.

Thoughts?

Thanks again!

comment_data.body:
Hi!

The suggested way of having custom ways to jump is to indeed create a mapping and use `MiniJump2d.start()` directly. As described [here](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/2431902e78b76f435542d1e606f08475360068ca/doc/mini-jump2d.txt#L339-L340).

> So, mapping all the modes myself seemed a bit worse.

That's not too bad and can be done relatively concisely. Here is what [I am using](https://github.com/echasnovski/nvim/blob/b7391abbe9a06c09322b7dd513c14c25286b59fd/plugin/30_mini.lua#L279-L285) right now in a wake of improving/rewriting 'mini.jump2d' (see #1818). I am fairly certain that those will be the new defaults ("single_character" variant as a default spotter).

So as there is a rewrite planned, things will (hopefully) be both more configurable and require less configuration to be good :).

---

> I'm not sure also of the nuance of this things, as operator pending mode is usually a thing that scares me a bit. :-)

It is not that scary when you get to know it :) It is a mode that activates after you start an operator (action that requires a target), like by pressing `d` or `c` or `y`, etc. This is usually followed by a textobject (like `i)`, `a"`, etc.) or a motion (like `t)` or `e`). The 'mini.jump2d' is a jumping plugin, so creating an Operator-pending mode mapping for it would allow to have something like 1) press `d`; 2) initial the jump; 3) finish the jump -> all the text from the cursor to the jump is deleted.
